answer: Admission runs only through bonded gateways called wharfs, each listed in a public atlas with its bond and per-epoch endorsement quota. Every identity's vine - the graph linking it back to the wharf that admitted it - is traced by auditors each cycle. A vine rooted in fake accounts gets the wharf's bond slashed and its whole batch demoted. Attackers pay twice: a fresh bond per fake wharf, and per-identity cost, since quotas forbid bulk discounts. Honest users pay one small fee once.
